walkthrough: Goal: keep painting when the tablet's GPU resets, and open a dense painting without the app freezing or losing its display; nothing drawn is ever lost.
Entry: open OpenPaint on the tablet (2880 x 1800, landscape); draw two lines with the Ink Pen.

A dense painting: a piece holding hundreds of textured strokes over one place opens from its card. The canvas fills in over a moment, whole tiles at a time from the top, never a tile half drawn; meanwhile taps, panels and two-finger navigation answer. Undo or redo of a large change, a layer or mask change and a merge fill in the same way. No frame asks the GPU for more than about a tenth of a second of work, so the system never resets it for running too long.

A GPU reset (the driver lost the device): within a moment the screen comes back, the canvas exactly as it was, the panels and tools as they were. A quiet pill in the top band says "The display was reset." with OK; tapping OK, or starting the next stroke, lets it go. A stroke the pen was drawing at that moment goes on under the pen and is committed whole at the lift, as if nothing happened; nothing the hand did is lost.
History survives: undo and redo step through the strokes drawn before and after the reset; leaving the app and coming back shows the same canvas.

Memory: when the GPU's memory runs short (zoomed in on a large busy artwork with many smudges and blurs), the app first lets the sharp zoom tiles go (the canvas shows magnified, softer, until there is room), then its quick-drawing copies of layers (strokes over a busy place draw a little slower), then smudge and blur results the canvas no longer shows, then the layer pictures; the canvas itself always stays exact.
Failure: if the GPU keeps resetting (more than three times a minute), the app stops making its display again and shows what it last could; the artwork is saved as always.
